headline: Dollar Tree beat with 4.2% comps from bigger tickets; higher-income households drove much of its new-customer growth.

metrics.comp_label: Dollar Tree comparable store net sales (continuing ops)

guidance_note: FY25 adj. EPS raised to $5.60-5.80; Q4 comps guided +4-6%, adj. EPS $2.40-2.60.
key_messages: Comps +4.2%: ticket +4.5%, traffic -0.3% (first traffic decline since FY2022).
Discretionary comps +4.8% vs consumables +3.5%; discretionary mix up 40 bps to 50.5%; record Halloween.
Gross margin +40 bps to 35.8% on mark-on and freight, offset by tariffs, markdowns and shrink.
About 3 million new households added, roughly 60% from middle- and higher-income consumers.
Family Dollar now reported as discontinued operations.

consumer.income_split: Roughly 60% of ~3 million new households came from middle- and higher-income consumers; higher earners shop less often, weighing on traffic.
consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary outperformed with a record Halloween and the first positive discretionary mix shift since Q1 2022.
consumer.pricing: Multi-price initiatives lifted mark-on; higher tariff costs partly offset.

macro_read: Higher-income households trading down are reshaping dollar-store growth, consistent with a K-shaped consumer and broad affordability strain.

sources.label: Dollar Tree Q3 FY2025 release (Business Wire)
Fortune: Rich people flooding dollar stores
